parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is national, not merely local: federal entry screening can refuse visa/passport mismatch and impose lifetime fraud findings; federal immigration/corrections custody has documented severe abuse; national facility rules and hostile counterterrorism framing affect trans travellers, especially if outed. The division's no facility ban, local ordinances, governor vetoes, adult care availability and marriage recognition reduce street/service friction for adults travelling alone. But those protections do not shield federal borders, funded facilities, immigration enforcement or minor-care funding pressure. Travelling families/minors face additional care denial, record subpoenas, and school/teacher exposure. Overall severity is high with uncertain remedies, placing it near high risk rather than severe.

entry_documents.exposure: National visa/entry guidance directs officers to refuse or seek evidence when documents/records mismatch assigned sex and to weigh material misrepresentation for lifetime ineligibility; reports of traveller passport blocking/confiscation and allied advisories show friction.
entry_documents.protection: Travelers use home passports, so national passport issuance rules are not a direct service; litigation, legal-aid guidance and some court challenges can contest refusals.
entry_documents.interaction: Document/name/sex mismatch can trigger secondary inspection and potentially removal/custody; local nondiscrimination rules do not pre-empt federal visa screening.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal immigration custody documented forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse; national corrections bureau adopted policies removing hormones and coercive psychiatric therapy; counts stopped.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No reliable visitor-facing remedy is documented for detention; court challenges may restrain some orders but not custody practice.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry refusal, fraud allegations or unrelated arrest can place travellers in federal custody where birth-sex expectations increase abuse risk.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities and defines sex binary; four other divisions criminalize facility use with documented arrest.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This division has no facility ban, no sex-definition law, and local ordinances cover employment, housing and public accommodation for part of population.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local permission does not shield federal/funded buildings; traveller may still be removed or criminalized elsewhere.

care_services.exposure: National funding freeze and public-insurance reimbursement denial caused two major division hospital systems to pause youth gender-affirming pharmacologic care; youth services shut down.
care_services.protection: Adult care is not state-banned; governor vetoed minor care ban; mental health continued; state officials challenged federal payments policy.
care_services.interaction: Adult travellers may access private care, but minor caregivers face denial, chilling effects and provider caution.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism prioritizes rapid identification and neutralization of radically pro-transgender groups; DOJ guidance invokes radical gender ideology; officials stopped counting trans prisoners.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; state service nondiscrimination executive order and some police anti-misgendering practices.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile framing can embolden border and police actions while local recourse is partial and often SO-based.

minors_guardians.exposure: National school investigation directive criminalizes teacher facilitation of social transition; subpoenas of under-19 medical records may chill care seeking.
minors_guardians.protection: Division has no statewide minor care ban; recognizes marriage and adoption rights; offers gender-neutral parent certificates.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling parent/guardian may be forced to disclose child status to access care, schooling or shelter while state protection cannot guarantee federal funding.

street_violence_police_response.protection: Partial local ordinances, dated supportive poll, police de-misgendering step; national hate-crime statute.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Protection depends on municipality; absence of current incident data leaves uncertainty despite some local recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Legal status changes by travel date; enforcement and hospital-pause status uncertain; short stays make complaints impractical.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Lawsuits, multistate coalition, running legal-aid FAQ; some orders blocked.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: National/local split creates conflicting obligations and slow remedies.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar universal border exposure and refusal; here worse because immigration-custody abuse and lifetime fraud are possible, but slightly less mechanical because no explicit trans ban and division has local protections.
Above 0.25-A: no documented raids, public-decency targeting, shelter exclusion or routine extortion; below low risk because federal border and custody severity remain substantial.
Materially below 0.75-C: national entry rules no longer accept matching markers or respectful screening, and local equality cannot pre-empt federal border, custody or funding consequences.

parsed.synthesis: National passport/visa discrepancy rules make discovery at entry a plausible universal exposure; refusal or fraud allegations can escalate to immigration custody, where severe abuse is documented. Local division protections—no bathroom ban, nondiscrimination ordinances, vetoes of youth-care bans, adult care access—lower day-to-day risk for adults alone. But federal facility and funding policies, hostile counterterrorism framing, and school/prosecution directives limit those gains and hit minors hardest: major hospital systems paused youth pharmacologic care after national reimbursement threats, and parents/schools face record subpoenas and criminalized support. Remedies exist but are litigation-bound, slow, and geographically patchy, so risk remains elevated.
